paragraphs.text: The chief city of Ephraim, near to old Joshua, who called this parliament thither, and not far from mount Gerizim and mount Ebal, where the people had lately renewed their covenant, which they were now to do again; and the identity of the place might be some advantage: whence it is that they that give rules of direction concerning prayer, do advise us, amongst other helps, to accustom ourselves to the same place.
paragraphs.anchor: And Joshua gathered all the tribes to Shechem.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Before the ark brought hither for the purpose.
paragraphs.anchor: And they presented themselves before God

paragraphs.text: Besides what he had said to them in the former chapter; so solicitous was he of the public welfare after his decease also. Cicero saith that this was his chiefest care: we are sure it was good Joshua’s.
paragraphs.anchor: And Joshua said unto all the people.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Of the river Euphrates, that ancient river. And this was the ancient manner of speaking to the people, by giving them a historical narrative of what God had done for them and their forefathers, that mercy might enforce to duty; since divine blessings are binders, and men’s offences are increased by their obligations. See the like method made use of by those admirable preachers, David, {Psa 78:1-72} Stephen, {Act 7:2-53} and Paul. {Act 13:17-41}
paragraphs.anchor: Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood

paragraphs.text: Even Abraham as well as the rest, {a} till God gave him a call out of his own country, till he had "called him to his foot," {Isa 41:2} that is, to follow him and his direction, to obey him without solicitation.
paragraphs.anchor: And they served other gods.

paragraphs.text: {a} Some of the Rabbis say that Terah got his living by making and selling of images.
Effaetae fidei filium, the heir of the covenant, and therein more happy than his brother Ishmael, with all those twelve princes which he begot. {Gen 17:20-21}
paragraphs.anchor: And gave him Isaac.

paragraphs.text: Where they were held under hard servitude, while Esau and his posterity flourished in mount Seir, having the fat of the earth’s good store, that they might fry the better in hell.
paragraphs.anchor: But Jacob and his children went down into Egypt.

paragraphs.text: As brands out of the fire; as many of you here present as were then under twenty years of age: and a great mercy it was to be pulled out of such a superstitious place. Gregory Nazianzen reporteth of Athens, that it was the most plagueful place in the world for superstition, even another Egypt. And he acknowledgeth it a great mercy that God did deliver him and Basil from those infections.
paragraphs.anchor: And I brought you out.

paragraphs.text: Yea, into the Red Sea God made them a fair way till they were in the midst, and then overcovered them. {Jos 24:7}
paragraphs.anchor: Unto the Red Sea.

paragraphs.text: Where ye had pluviam escatilem et petram aquatilem, as Tertullian phraseth it: never was prince so served in his greatest pomp as ye were all that while.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye dwelt in the wilderness a long season.

paragraphs.text: Whose iniquity was now grown full, {Gen 15:16} and come up to a just measure of merit of extraordinary vengeance from above. The bottle of wickedness, when once filled with those bitter waters, will surely sink to the bottom.
paragraphs.anchor: And I brought you into the land of the Amorites.

paragraphs.text: Then Balak … arose and warred against Israel.] He did not actually war against them. {Jdg 11:25} Sed fieri dicitur quod tentatur aut intenditur, saith Ribera upon Amo 9:5. He did not, because he durst not. Howbeit, because he intended, if he could have compassed it, to fight with Israel, and prepared for that purpose, it is spoken of as a done thing. So Haman is said to have "laid his hands upon the Jews," because he attempted it; {Est 8:7} and the Jews to have stoned Christ, because they could have found in their hearts to have done it. {Joh 10:31-33}
“Qui, quid non potuit, non facit, ille facit.”

Though full sore against his mind, as loath to lose so fair a preferment; till at length he resolved to curse, whatever came of it, and therefore went not, as at other times, to his altar, but "set his face toward the wilderness." {Num 24:1-2} "Howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing," said that good Nehemiah. {Neh 13:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore he blessed you still

paragraphs.text: Non pugnarunt, sed clausis portis propugnarunt et restiterunt, saith Vatablus. They shut up their gates and fortified themselves against you; and when their town was taken, it is probable they sold their lives at as dear a rate as they could.
paragraphs.anchor: And the men of Jericho fought against you.

paragraphs.text: Crabrones, sive muscam venenatam: Metaphorice de terrore illis incusso, saith Piscator; It is to be metaphorically taken for stinging terrors, struck into the hearts of these Canaanites. But why not literally rather?
paragraphs.anchor: And I sent the hornet before you.

paragraphs.text: But with my hornets.
paragraphs.anchor: But not with thy sword.

paragraphs.text: For Hazor only was burnt, {Jos 11:13} and the rest inhabited by them.
paragraphs.anchor: And cities which ye built not.

paragraphs.text: Deastros illos, which some of them secretly worshipped, as they did likewise in the wilderness. {Amo 5:25-26 Act 7:42-43} So in Josiah’s days, Baal had privily his "Chemarims," or chimney chaplains, yea, those that "worshipped the host of heaven upon the housetops," &c. {Zep 1:4-5}
paragraphs.anchor: And put away the gods.

paragraphs.text: He leaveth them not to their own free choice to do either, but to make proof of their voluntary and professed subjection to the true religion, which would further engage them to constancy in their covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: Choose you this day whom ye will serve.

paragraphs.text: Joshua was not of the mind of most householders in these days, who make no other use of their servants than they do of their beasts; while they may have their bodies to do their service, they care not if their souls serve the devil: these forget that they must answer for those souls, and give an account of their blood.
paragraphs.anchor: But as for me and my house.

paragraphs.text: And yet they did thus, not long after Joshua’s death. It is ordinary with the many headed multitude to turn with the stream, to tack about to every wind, to be of the same religion with others their superiors, to keep on the sunny side, wheresoever it be. Thus at Rome in Dioclesian’s time they were Pagans; in Constantine’s, Christians; in Constantius’s, Arians; in Julian’s, Apostates; in Jovinian’s, Christians again; and all this within less than the age of a man. It is therefore "a good thing that the heart be established with grace," {Heb 13:9} that men may "cleave to God with full purpose," {Act 11:23} being "steadfast and unmovable." {1Co 15:58}
paragraphs.anchor: God forbid that we should forsake the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Beneficium postulat officium; Mercy requireth duty: deliverance commandeth obedience. But many miscreants, as if God had hired them to be wicked, abuse all his benefits to his dishonour.
paragraphs.anchor: He it is that brought us up.

paragraphs.text: To make the Lord to be our God, it is required, saith a reverend man, that with highest estimations, most vigorous affections, and utmost endeavours we bestow ourselves upon him: so shall we be in a condition to "serve him acceptably." {Heb 12:28}
paragraphs.anchor: We will also serve the Lord; for he is our God.

paragraphs.text: You that are yet unregenerate, and that would fain make a mixture of religions, cannot serve the Lord; for he must be served like himself, that is, truly, that there be no halting; and totally, that there be no halving; he will not take up with a seeming or slubbering service. "Offer it now to thy prince; will he be pleased with thee or accept thy person? saith the Lord of hosts." {Mal 1:8}
paragraphs.anchor: Ye cannot serve the Lord.

paragraphs.text: And requireth to be sanctified in all those that draw near unto him; it will be worse with them else. {Lev 10:3} Neither profaneness nor formal profession will he endure; but least of all idolatry.
paragraphs.anchor: For he is a holy God.

paragraphs.text: And will not be yoked with idols, neither will he give his glory, which is as his wife, to another. If any cast but a leering look toward it, he shall smart and smoke for so doing.
paragraphs.anchor: For he is a jealous God.

paragraphs.text: sc., Unless you forego them: or if he do forgive them, yet he may take vengeance, temporal vengeance, of their inventions; {Psa 99:8} and for that matter their repentance may come too late. {Deu 1:37 2Sa 12:16} All this Joshua speaketh, not to weaken but to waken their diligence in God’s service.
paragraphs.anchor: He will not forgive your transgressions

paragraphs.text: Ingentia beneficia, flagitia, supplicia. From apostates God will take away his own and be gone, {Hos 2:9} he will curse their blessings, {Mal 2:2} blast their hopes, make them know the worth of his benefits by the want of them, making them cry out, as Jer 4:13, "Woe to us! for we are spoiled."
paragraphs.anchor: And consume you, after that he hath done you good.

paragraphs.text: Only and wholly, for subject and object. This was well resolved, if as well practised. These here were ready to enter into covenant, and so to bind their deceitful hearts to a good abearance, which else would be ready to slip collar.
paragraphs.anchor: Nay; but we will serve the Lord.

paragraphs.text: In case ye falsify ye shall be self-condemned, and cut of your own mouths God shall judge you: meanwhile conscience shall do its office upon you, as an index, iudex, vindex, accuser, judge, and executioner.
paragraphs.anchor: Ye are witnesses against yourselves.

paragraphs.text: Set forthwith upon the work of reformation which you have covenanted.
paragraphs.anchor: Now therefore.

paragraphs.text: Out of doors with those Balaam’s blocks, those mawmets and monuments of idolatry, those images of jealousy which provoke to jealousy: {Eze 8:3} throw also all your sinful lusts out of service, and serve the Lord. See Jos 24:14.
paragraphs.anchor: Put away the strange.

paragraphs.text: They bind themselves again to keep touch with God by an unalterable resolution. Vows rightly made and renewed are of singular use to keep the heart within the bounds of obedience, and to make men constant, firm, and peremptory in well doing.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord our God will we serve.

paragraphs.text: Capita faederis ex Deuteronomio praelegit, saith one; he read them the Articles of the Covenant out of Deuteronomy.
paragraphs.anchor: And set there a statute and an ordinance.

paragraphs.text: This whole book, or the most part of it, {see Jos 1:1} and particularly the Acts of this present Parliament.
paragraphs.anchor: And Joshua wrote these words.

paragraphs.text: Which was therehence called The Oak or Plain of the Pillar. {Jdg 9:6}
paragraphs.anchor: Under an oak.

paragraphs.text: It shall represent your covenant to your consciences, and convince you of singular perfidy, in case you falsify. We read in Livy that a certain governor of the people called Aequi, bade the Roman ambassadors tell their tale to the oak that stood next them, saying that he had somewhat else to do than to give them audience. To whom they replied, Et haec sacrata quercus audiat faedus a vobis violatum, Then let this holy oak hear and bear witness that ye have broken your covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us.

paragraphs.text: With their hearts full of joy at the covenant. "For they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire," as 2Ch 15:15.
paragraphs.anchor: So Joshua let the people depart.

paragraphs.text: Joshua … the servant of the Lord, died.] This was the crown of all his commendation, and a greater title to be engraven on his tomb, than his was, who arrogantly and foolishly styled himself Kοσμοκρατωρ, Monarch of the World. This was Sesostris, king of Egypt, who reigned there in the days of Samson.

Where his monument was to be seen in Jerome’s time, as he testifieth in his questions upon Genesis.
paragraphs.anchor: Buried they in Shechem.

paragraphs.text: Or, In Gibeathpineas, the name of a city, bearing his name.
paragraphs.anchor: In a hill that pertained to Phinehas.

paragraphs.text: By the synagogue, saith Vatablus, in an extraordinary way; that, being the high priest, he might be near to Joshua, and not far from the tabernacles where his business lay.
